For older adults, consuming enough protein to minimize age-associated loss in muscle mass is important. The 
recommendation for protein intake includes 23–31 oz per week at the minimum or 35% of total calories (Molfino et 
al., 2021; U.S. Department of Agriculture, 2020). Continuous anorexia in frail older adults negatively impacts their 
body composition; to combat this problem, early nutritional intervention improves outcomes and quality of life 
(Molfino et al., 2021). Like all age groups, older adults should strive to choose nutrient-rich foods. The ability to 
absorb Vitamin B12 decreases with age and the use of certain medications, so ensuring adequate intake of this 
vitamin is of particular concern (U.S. Department of Agriculture, 2020).
